decisiveStep.step: Substitute the known root of the divisor f(x) into the supplied division identity to eliminate its unknown quotient and recover f(4).
decisiveStep.reason: x=−2를 f(x²)=f(x)Q(x)+10x+2에 넣어 f(4)=−18을 얻고 f=(x+2)(x−k)의 k를 결정한다.

l4Cluster.label: Evaluate a supplied division identity
l4Cluster.skeleton: Substitute the requested input into a supplied dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder identity; use another input if needed to recover a quotient value.
l4Cluster.reason: The supplied dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder identity is evaluated at a strategically chosen input that nulls the quotient term, matching C04.

decisiveStep.step: Extract coefficients in ascending powers of x−2 by repeated synthetic division at the shift center 2.
decisiveStep.reason: x=2를 세 차례 조립제법 중심으로 사용해 d,c,b와 마지막 몫 a를 차례로 읽는다.

l4Cluster.skeleton: For an identity in powers of x−r, apply synthetic division repeatedly at r to extract coefficients from constant term upward.
l4Cluster.reason: Repeated coefficient extraction in the translated basis is the exact C11 skeleton; only the center and final expression differ.

l4Cluster.reason: The essential procedure is the same iterative leading-term cancellation as C07; blank placement is display format.

solutionMathEvidence: The solution evaluates at x=−2, transfers f(−2)=3, and gets (−2)²·3=12.

decisiveStep.step: Evaluate the dividend x²f(x) at the root −2 of the monic linear divisor to obtain the constant remainder.
decisiveStep.reason: f(−2)=3이므로 x²f(x)의 −2에서 값은 4·3이며 이는 x+2 나머지와 같다.

l4Cluster.label: Linear-divisor root evaluation
l4Cluster.skeleton: Evaluate the dividend at a monic linear divisor root to obtain its constant remainder; if it is zero, use exact factorization to evaluate the quotient, and for integer residues verify the standard range.
l4Cluster.reason: This is the root-value remainder transfer in C01 with no quotient follow-up; multiplying by x² only changes the value evaluated.

sourceIssue.reason: 주어진 기존 나머지와 새 dividend x²f(x), 같은 divisor x+2가 명확해 한 점 대입으로 바로 해결된다.

sourceMathEvidence: The monic cubic P has equal quotient and remainder when divided by x²−4; additionally, (x+2)P is divisible by x²−4.
solutionMathEvidence: Writing the common linear quotient/remainder as x+t gives P=(x²−4+1)(x+t); the additional factor condition forces P(2)=0 and hence t=−2.

primaryMethod.method: equal quotient-remainder factorization with root condition
primaryMethod.reason: 공통 몫·나머지 일차식을 하나의 미지식으로 두고 외부의 나누어떨어짐 조건으로 그 계수를 정한다.

decisiveStep.step: Set the common quotient and remainder equal to one linear polynomial, factor P as (divisor+1) times that polynomial, then apply the extra root condition.
decisiveStep.reason: P=(x²−4+1)(x+t)를 이용하고 (x+2)P의 x²−4 나눗셈에서 추가로 P(2)=0임을 적용한다.

l4Cluster.label: Equal quotient-remainder factorization with independent root constraint
l4Cluster.skeleton: Set the common quotient and remainder S equal; write P=DS+S=(D+1)S, use the remainder-degree/monicity constraints where needed, then apply a separate known root or divisibility condition to fix the remaining parameter.
l4Cluster.reason: This shares the quotient-equals-remainder factorization with q2; the independent root condition fixes the remaining parameter. It is bounded apart from C05’s linked multiple-division compatibility.

sourceIssue.reason: 몫=나머지, monic cubic 조건, (x+2)P의 추가 나누어떨어짐 및 목표값 P(3)이 모두 원문에 있어 t가 정해진다.

sourceMathEvidence: The monic cubic has equal remainders at x+1 and x−2, and f(2x−1)+f(x) is divisible by x(x−1).
solutionMathEvidence: The solution translates the first condition to f(−1)=f(2), and the second to values at x=0,1; these yield two linear equations for A,B and C.

primaryMethod.method: recover cubic coefficients from point-value constraints
primaryMethod.reason: 두 인수 x, x−1의 근에서 함수값 관계를 얻고, 나머지 등식과 함께 삼차식 계수 연립식을 푼다.

decisiveStep.step: Evaluate the divisibility identity at its roots 0 and 1 and combine those function values with f(−1)=f(2) to solve the cubic coefficients.
decisiveStep.reason: x=1에서 f(1)=0, x=0에서 f(−1)+f(0)=0을 얻고, f(−1)=f(2)와 함께 A,B,C를 푼다.

l4Cluster.label: Low-degree value interpolation

l4Cluster.reason: A low-degree polynomial is reconstructed from a small set of point-value constraints, the same repeatable coefficient-recovery core as C02.
